checksums.name: header_checksum
checksums.formula_detail: Additive 16-bit checksum over big-endian u16 words (driver assembles each u16 MSB-first). stored_word7 = (-(sum of BE u16 words 0..6)) mod 65536; valid iff sum of all 8 BE u16 words mod 65536 == 0. LE sum of samples is 0x01FE (fails), BE sum is 0x0000 (passes).

checksums.name: slot_checksum
checksums.formula_detail: Same additive 16-bit BE u16 sum over the full 2040-byte slot (1020 words, FUN_08038010(buf, 0x7F8) in FUN_08037f4c); slot valid iff total mod 65536 == 0, so the final word must hold the negated partial sum. Both samples: every slot sums to 0xFC18 (20 zero words + 1000 unwritten 0xFFFF words), correctly marking all slots empty. Stored-word position (final word) inferred, not observed on a valid slot.

io_driver_functions.notes: DMA3 transfer primitive: writes src/dst to DMA3 registers (0x040000D4 block), count|0x80000000 to DMA3 control, busy-waits on bit 0x8000. Used for every EEPROM bitstream transfer to/from 0x0D000000.

EEPROM read one 8-byte block: DMA-out addr_bits+3 command halfwords (address MSB-first, leading bits 1,1) to 0x0D000000, DMA-in 0x44 halfwords, reassembles 4 u16 MSB-first. Rejects block >= config block count.

EEPROM write one 8-byte block: expands 4 u16 to 64 bits MSB-first plus address bits with leading 0,1 opcode, DMAs addr_bits+0x43 halfwords to 0x0D000000, then busy-polls 0x0D000000 bit0 with timer budget 0x88.
Write-verify: reads block back via 0x0804ca54 and compares 4 u16; returns 0 on match, 0x8000 on mismatch.
Write wrapper gated on config device-type word != 0x200, delegating to 0x0804cb18.
Write-with-verify, up to 3 attempts of 0x0804cd10 + 0x0804cc78. Entry point for all EEPROM writes.
EEPROM timing/type configuration (called with 0x40 by the bus lock). Branches on 4 / 0x40 / other to select timing globals.
Bus lock: saves/masks control globals and calls 0x0804c98c(0x40) before a block burst.
Bus unlock: restores the control global saved by 0x0803812c.
Read N blocks (start_block, count, ram_dst); 8 bytes per block, lock/unlock bracketed. Slot load uses (slot*0xFF+2, 0xFF, buf).
Write N blocks via 0x0804cd48 per block, 8 bytes per block. Traced uses: header (0,2) and 5-block slot stubs only; no full-slot (0xFF-block) call site recovered.
Additive u16 checksum: sums byte_len/2 consecutive u16 words into a 16-bit accumulator.
Create default header: memcpy 16-byte ROM template to header mirror, store -sum at word 7 (+0x0E), write blocks 0-1.
Validate header: read blocks 0-1; return 1 iff 8-word sum == 0 and first 8 bytes match the '0000EISA' magic.
Flush header: zero mirror +0x0E, recompute via 0x08038010, store negation; write blocks 0-1 only if mirror first u32 == EEPROM header first u32. Returns 1 on flush.
Load one slot: 0x080380cc(slot*0xFF+2, 0xFF, work buffer) = 2040 bytes.
Validate one slot: valid flag at mgr+0xB4+slot = (0x08038010(buf, 0x7F8) == 0).
Zero the 2040-byte slot work buffer (memset helper 0x08027af0).
Enumerate 4 slots: load+validate each; zero the 40-byte descriptor of invalid slots, else hand descriptor to out-of-cluster parser func_0x0801bbac.
Boot init (no caller in callgraph; jumptable entry): alloc zeroed 2040-byte buffer, validate header, on failure create header + write 5-block zero stubs at blocks 2/257/512/767, then enumerate slots.
Writes mgr byte +10 = FUN_080450dc() getter value and mgr byte +11 = 1 immediately before the header flush in the 0x0802417c chain. Exact .sav offset mapping unproven.

fields.name: header_magic
fields.update_mechanism: Written from the 16-byte ROM template at initialisation; byte-compared (8 bytes) on validation and gated by first u32 ('0000') before any flush.
fields.evidence: Bytes 30 30 30 30 45 49 53 41 at offset 0 of both .sav files; 8-byte compare loop in FUN_08038074 and first-u32 compare in FUN_08037fb4.

fields.name: header_byte_08
fields.update_mechanism: Changed -1 between the two sequential captures while byte 0x0C changed +1, preserving the header checksum. Candidate path is a header-mirror mutation flushed by FUN_08037fb4 in the FUN_0802417c chain; exact writer not identified.
fields.evidence: Byte diff 0x08: 07->06 and 0x0C: 00->01 in saves/hexdump_and_diffs.txt; BE checksum unchanged (0xFF80) in both files.

fields.name: header_byte_09_const
fields.update_mechanism: Part of the checksummed header template; never observed to change. Read only via the header checksum.
fields.evidence: 0x96 in both samples; covered by the verified header checksum (FUN_08038010/FUN_08038074).

fields.name: header_bytes_0A_0B
fields.update_mechanism: Candidate only: FUN_08037d3c writes manager bytes +10 = FUN_080450dc() and +11 = 1 immediately before the header flush, but the manager base pointer is unresolved, so identity with header bytes 0x0A/0x0B is unproven (a flushed +11=1 would contradict the observed 00).
fields.evidence: FUN_08037d3c body writes at +10/+11; both saves show 00 00 at 0x0A-0x0B.

fields.name: header_byte_0C
fields.update_mechanism: Changed +1 between captures, exactly compensating byte 0x08 in the BE checksum. Semantics unknown; exact writer not identified.
fields.evidence: Byte diff 0x0C: 00->01; stored header checksum identical (FF 80) in both files.

fields.name: header_byte_0D
fields.update_mechanism: Checksummed template byte; never observed to change.
fields.evidence: 0x00 in both samples; covered by the verified header checksum.

fields.name: header_checksum
fields.update_mechanism: Zeroed, region summed with FUN_08038010, negated sum stored. Byte order in the file is big-endian (first byte 0xFF is the high byte, value 0xFF80); the schema type enum has no BE u16 variant, so type is bytes with the BE interpretation stated here and in the checksums section.
fields.evidence: Python: BE sum of all 8 words == 0x0000 and stored == -sum(first 7) == 0xFF80 on both files; LE sum == 0x01FE fails. Code: FUN_08038034 '_DAT_0803806c[7] = -sVar1', FUN_08037fb4 '*(short*)(mirror+0xE) = -sVar2'.

fields.update_mechanism: Inferred final-word position: offset shown is slot_0 base (16) + 2038 = 2054 in file terms for slot 0; each slot's stored word is at its own base+2038. fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip one bit, no checksum repair
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Discriminates boot order: either full re-initialisation to template header (FUN_08038074 fails) or in-place re-checksum via the FUN_0802417c -> FUN_08037fb4 flush (first u32 '0000' intact), consistent with the PACKET probe where a 0x08 mutation was not reverted.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Corrupt one magic byte, then repair header checksum
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Full re-initialisation despite valid checksum, proving the 8-byte magic is checked independently in FUN_08038074.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Corrupt one 'EISA'-half magic byte, then repair header checksum
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If re-initialised, the full 8-byte compare is operative; if the save survives, only the first-u32 gate matters and the FUN_08038074 compare operands are ambiguous in decompilation.

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Slot 0 becomes selectable/loadable; recording which payload offsets change the menu descriptor (parser func_0x0801bbac) begins mapping the unknown slot-internal layout.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Same fill as the valid-slot test but omit slot checksum repair
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Slot 0 still shows empty (valid flag mgr+0xB4 stays 0, descriptor zeroed), proving validity is checksum-only on this path.

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Slot 0 becomes empty again, confirming the stored slot checksum sits in the final word.

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Any UI/default-state difference vs cap-00 reveals the semantics of the only two observed mutable header bytes; no difference implies opaque versioning bytes.

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Boot re-initialises; diffing the rewritten file against cap-00 isolates which header bytes come from the ROM template vs runtime state, recovering true birth values of bytes 0x08-0x0D.
No observable change; game never reads or rewrites the tail.

open_questions: No populated save slot exists in the corpus: both samples are freshly initialised (header + 40-byte zero stubs). The entire internal layout of the 2040-byte slot payload is unknown and cannot be mapped clean-room from these files.

No full-slot gameplay writer was recovered among the 260 decompiled functions: the only slot writes traced are the 5-block initialisation stubs. The writer that serialises gameplay state into the 2040-byte buffer, sets its final checksum word, and calls FUN_080380fc(slot*0xFF+2, 0xFF, buf) is missing, likely behind an UNRECOVERED_JUMPTABLE edge.

Exact EWRAM mirror addresses are unresolvable: all mirrors are reached through unresolved ROM literal pointers (_DAT_0803xxxx) and no ROM image is in the workspace, so ram_addr is null for every field.

Header bytes 0x08 and 0x0C changed in a checksum-compensating pair between captures (07->06, 00->01); their semantics (counters, settings, versioning) and their exact writer are unknown. FUN_08037d3c's manager +10/+11 writes could not be proven to land on header bytes 0x0A/0x0B.

The EEPROM config struct values (block-count limit at cfg+4, timing at cfg+6, address-bit count at cfg+8) live in ROM and are not in the workspace; the 10-bit block addressing for 1024 blocks is inferred from the 8192-byte media size.

FUN_08038074's 8-byte magic compare operands (iRam080380c4 vs iRam080380c8) are unresolved Ghidra RAM constants; which side is the ROM '0000EISA' constant vs the read buffer cannot be distinguished from the decompilation alone (fuzzing target at offset 4 discriminates).

The descriptor parser func_0x0801bbac called by FUN_08037c70 for valid slots is outside the 260 decompiled bodies; how it interprets the loaded 2040-byte buffer (names, timestamps, progress shown in the menu) is unknown.
No paired .ss save states ship in states/, so none of the fuzzing predictions in this report have been executed; all remain to be tested by reloading mutated saves.
